entries.answer: A noun typically refers to a person, place, thing, concept or entity.
A verb typically expresses an action, occurrence, state or relation.
An adjective typically modifies a noun or noun phrase by describing a property or quality.
Translation expresses the meaning of a source text in another language.
An adverb commonly modifies a verb, adjective, another adverb or an entire clause.
A pronoun is a word or expression that can substitute for or refer to a noun phrase.
A preposition commonly expresses a relation between a following noun phrase and another part of a sentence.
A sentence is a grammatical unit capable of expressing a complete proposition or speech act depending on context.
An alphabet is a writing system using a set of symbols representing phonemes or related sound units.
Grammar is the system of rules and patterns governing the structure of a language.
